stem: Harsh tips fallen leaves and kitchen scraps into a sealed garden bin. Weeks later the waste has become dark, crumbly manure.

parts.text: Which claim correctly explains the change?

options.text: Bacteria and fungi break the plant waste down into simpler nutrient-rich manure.
The waste becomes manure on its own, and then microorganisms arrive to feed on it.
Microorganisms produce biogas from the waste in an open, well-aerated heap.

parts.text: Name one useful product of that breakdown.

part_answers.answer: Nutrient-rich manure that can enrich soil.

teacher.key_rationale: Soil microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi break plant waste into nutrient-rich manure. Manure does not form first and then attract microbes, and biogas needs oxygen-free conditions rather than an open well-aerated heap.
